title-proc.eng: Pre-qualification to Restricted Tenderer Panel for Howth FHC Dredging Project At Howth Fishery Harbour Centre, Dublin

description-proc.eng: The Howth FHC Dredging Project is a €30m+ project to dredge the harbour involves the dredging, stabilisation and beneficial reuse of circa 240,000 cubic metres of contaminated but non-hazardous bed material. This material is located within the confines of the West and East piers of Howth harbour in four main zones known as: * the fishing basin between West and Middle Piers * the channel which provides access from sea * the outer swing mooring area to the north of the inner break water * the inner Marina basin which is adjacent to the public slipway and channel It is proposed that this material is treated and stabilised using a pumped liquid mixing method in a location on the Middle Pier and pumped to a location to the West of the West Pier where it is to be used as the core infill of a new reclaimed multi use land area. In order to minimise delays and to give potential tenderers the best opportunity to tender for the overall project, the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine are undertaking a pre-qualification process to assess the suitability of prospective tenderers for the main construction and dredging contract relating to the Howth FHC Dredging works. The Department are proposing to prequalify the top 6 ranked applicants, with a minimum number of 3. Submissions are sought from suitably experienced applicants who can demonstrate experience relevant to the required works and who can mobilise sufficient plant and labour resources to undertake and complete the project. The works contract will be tendered in a two-stage format, with pre-qualification and suitability questionnaire stage commencing in May 2026 in order to generate a shortlist for the restricted final tender process to be undertaken. Prequal stage is expected to be complete in June/July 2026, with the restricted follow on stage to follow on shortly after.

title-proc.eng: Works contracts – Section 3 Paraćin – Trupale (design and build) for Railway Line under the Belgrade – Niš Railway Modernisation Project

description-proc.eng: The Works Contract covers Section 3 of the Belgrade–Niš Modernisation Project, which is divided into three subsections, (sub-section 3.2 Stalać – Đunis is already contracted). The works relate to Sub-sections 3.1 Paraćin–Stalać and 3.3 Đunis–Trupale. Sub-section Paraćin–Stalać is 20.8 km long, while Sub-section Đunis–Trupale is 37.7 km long. A total of nine stations will be reconstructed and modernised to meet the demands of both passenger and freight traffic. The design speed is 200 km/h for Sub-section 3.1 and 160 km/h for Sub-section 3.3. On Sub-section 3.1, works include 12 grade-separated crossings, 8 bridges and culverts, 2 pedestrian underpasses, 1 retaining wall, and 17 culvert structures beneath the railway track. On Sub-section 3.3, works include 18 grade-separated crossings, 14 bridges and culverts, 2 pedestrian underpasses, 15 retaining walls, 18 culvert structures beneath the railway track, and 2 culvert structures beneath roadways. Across both Sub-sections 3.1 and 3.3, works include reconstruction of the existing and construction of new overhead contact line (OCL) systems, as well as electrical power installations in stations, tunnels and tunnel entrances, energy facilities, relay stations, sectioning posts (including those with neutral sections), remote control systems for electric traction installations, transformer stations supplied from OCL, and lighting of grade-separated crossings and access roads. During the execution of signalling works in stations, automatic switching of turnouts and train routes will not be possible. Due to the shutdown of station signalling systems, operations will be adapted to a temporary mode. Inter-signal interlocking devices (UMZ) will be used, installed in temporary rooms for train dispatchers, with traffic managed within station areas. Some limited works on neighbouring sections may be included in the scope of the contract.
